scope: Independent static review of final common P47/P48 notification frontend/backend plus deterministic verification of author evidence. No application, real Agent, native notification, browser rerun, project test or Cargo execution by this reviewer.

source.baselineAccounting: Original backend receipt and checkpoint remain frozen. Seven of its eight source hashes still match; windows.rs is superseded only by windows-followup/receipt.json. Exact old Windows bytes are retained and match the original SHA. All twelve final frontend hashes match.

findingsClosed.finding: Disabling one reminder kind under system Denied must not erase the other unchanged saved preference.
findingsClosed.origin: Static review of private draft; not claimed as an installed production failure.
findingsClosed.resolution: Each requested false disables; unchanged true preserves the prior user choice; only false-to-true requires actual system permission. Delivery still checks real permission. Author targeted tests include both Denied directions.

findingsClosed.finding: Frontend current-owner checks before IPC cannot retire a submission already waiting behind backend awaits.
findingsClosed.resolution: Exact existing rendererNonce/sequence RAM ticket, pending-attempt ownership and explicit withdrawal span both sides. Actual session store publication invalidates the owner synchronously; success, approval and question share pending tracking. Late/unknown submit is not retried or called suppressed without a withdrawal receipt.

findingsClosed.finding: Windows DispatchStarted was set before fallible notice-map acquisition, which could return before Show.
findingsClosed.origin: Static source finding only; no Windows failure was executed.
findingsClosed.resolution: Map registration, release and old-notice cleanup now precede dispatch. The dispatch closure directly enters Show; withdrawal winning between registration and Show causes exact forget(id). Reviewed final minimal diff; owned rustfmt output is author evidence. No shared helper or unrelated code change.

reviewedInvariants: Old preference data decodes with independent default-off successEnabled; reads do not rewrite settings. Fixed notification body and reviewed diagnostic fields exclude Agent/user message contents.

Only actual send admission creates a success candidate. Exact thread object, connection, native session and current request boundary remain required. Official end_turn and actual projected done/reply or completed tool result are reconciled; active/unknown/failed/stopped task, pending permission, uncertain configuration, failed tool/compaction, replay and prose do not prove successful completion.

The bounded pending-attempt set handles new work, connection loss and removed exact store owner. Approval/question pending IDs are rechecked. Hiding the work view alone does not retire the owner; interruption is not guessed resolved from presentation fields.

Pending tickets are never evicted. Bounded renderer watermarks prevent old not-yet-admitted submit revival after early withdrawal, including terminal record eviction. High sequences reject older unadmitted IPC without invalidating a live lower-sequence ticket. Capacity refuses new work rather than dropping live ownership.

The platform closure/worker owns the ticket across observer timeout. The final ticket lock arbitrates withdrawal versus platform submission; preference revision, actual background state and target resolution are rechecked. macOS callback/diagnostic paths do not acquire this ticket lock, avoiding synchronous-callback self-deadlock.

withdrawn proves the exact request did not cross the dispatch boundary; alreadySubmitted only means native submission began, not API acceptance/display. unknown retains uncertainty. No automatic notification retry or persistent event/delivery ledger was added.

Final Windows notice registration does not hold the map mutex during Show or event cleanup. macOS FFI start/one callback and Box ownership remain separate from observer completion. Windows execution and installed macOS presentation remain unverified in this review.
